Saturated LP steam is added to the pre-heated BF gas to achieve a minimum steam-to-dry gas (S: DG) ratio of 0.5 at the exit of WGS reactors. The mixed process gas flows from top to bottom through the high- temperature CO-Shift WGS (high-temperature shift) reactors, which is filled with Iron-Chromium oxide catalyst (Vendor: Clariant). There are four parallel sets of reactors to handle the BF gas volume. The CO in the BF gas reacts with steam, forming H and CO according to CO-Shift Reaction: 2 2 CO + H O ↔ CO + H + Heat 2 2 2 The CO-Shift reaction is exothermic, which leads to a 230oF temperature rise depending upon the content of CO in the BF gas and the effectiveness of catalyst age. The CO-content at the outlet of the high- temperature shift (HTS) reactor is about 3.8 to 4 mol % (dry). In addition, the heat generated from the steam preheats the boiler feed water (BFW) in the downstream equipment. The main parameters to be controlled in the CO shift reactor are the S: DG ratio (to maintain the desired exothermicity) and the BF gas inlet temperature to the reactor. A steam-to-dry gas ratio of 0.5 (at the exit of WGS reactors) is achieved by flow control of the process steam to the system. At the outlet of the HTS reactor, the shifted gas enters two parallel sets of WGS boilers, where it is cooled while generating steam. The boiler is connected to the steam drum by risers and downcomers, enabling a natural circulation system. The primary objective of controlling the WGS boiler is maintaining the BFW level within the steam drum. A low drum level risks uncovering the boiler tubes and exposing them to heat stress and damage. High drum level risks of water carry-over into the steam header and exposing steam turbines to corrosion and wear. This control is done via three element control philosophy, where steam flow is measured together with boiler drum level and feed water flow. The feed-forward control keeps the feed water supply balanced with the steam demand. The drum level controller trims the feed water flow SP to compensate for errors in the flow measurements or any other unmeasured load disturbances (e.g., blowdown) that may affect the drum level. In the BFW preheater, BFW is heated with shifted hot gas exiting the WGS boiler. The temperature of the process gas is controlled by the BFW flow bypass across two parallel sets of exchangers. The remaining heat in the shifted gas is removed via the quench column. The shift gas quencher is a packed column where the shifted gas is cooled by direct contact with recirculated water; the cooling is controlled via the recirculation rate of the water.
